verdict: DRAM pricing cycle decelerating to +20% QoQ in Q4-2026 as all three HBM4 suppliers ramp capacity — baseline correction-risk window confirming; hyperscaler capex holding $720-745B with Q3 updates pending; chip stocks weak mid-Oct with NVDA -2.4%; optical InP constraint persisting through Q1-2027.
body_md:
## Fresh Developments (last 24–72h)

**Signal 1 — DRAM/HBM Pricing:** TrendForce (Oct 20) projects Q4-2026 conventional DRAM contract prices +~20% QoQ — marked deceleration from ~80% (Q2) and ~40% (Q3). Cited drivers: higher comparison base, weakening end-market purchasing power, and LTA price ceilings. HBM spot estimates: HBM3E 36GB stack ~$300, HBM4 ~$550–600 (secondary sources, unconfirmed).

**Signal 2 — HBM4 Ramp / Correction Risk:** All three suppliers scaling into late 2026 — confirming the baseline correction-risk window. Samsung: HBM4 >60% of HBM sales in H2-2026. Micron: targeting 100K wafers/month by year-end (vs. ~40–50K prior). SK Hynix M15X in volume ramp since Q1-2026. No news denying correction risk; supply divergence from demand increasingly visible into 2027.

**Signal 3 — Hyperscaler Capex:** 2026 aggregate guidance $720–745B (MSFT ~$175B, Alphabet ~$195–205B, Amazon ~$220B, Meta ~$130–145B). Q3 earnings updates pending — major hyperscalers report late October. No guide-down detected. Goldman synthesis puts the figure near $800B including Oracle.

**Signal 4 — AMD MI400 / Custom ASIC:** No fresh October catalysts. Background: AMD Helios (72× MI455X, 31 TB HBM4/rack) presented at Hot Chips 2026, full production, OpenAI and Meta onboarding Q4-2026. Google Ironwood (TPU7x) GA since March 2026; AWS Trainium3 GA.

**Signal 5 — Optical/Photonics:** No breaking news last 24h. Most recent catalyst was Oct 1 Bernstein Outperform initiation — COHR, LITE, CIEN each +6–7% that day. YTD: LITE +183%, COHR +73%, CIEN +62%. LITE 200G lasers sold out at ~2× prior-gen ASP; CPO revenue ~$50M Q4-2026 guide. COHR InP 6-inch capacity ramping; InP constraint expected through Q1-2027.

**Signal 6 — Solar:** No fresh FSLR/ENPH/NXT/ARRY news last 24–72h. Policy backdrop: US Section 232 tariffs on polysilicon effective Dec 4, 2026 — 15% tariff + price floors ($0.38/W modules). Module prices may rise to ~$0.40/W. Structural AI datacenter power demand tailwind intact.

**Signal 7 — Watchlist Movers:** NVDA -2.42% (~$216.59) on Oct 22, continuing mid-October weakness (AI-trade narrative; Wall St. targets unchanged ~$263). MRVL +6% Oct 19 on chip-sector rebound. AMD -0.62% Oct 20. No material news on MU, AVGO, ALAB, CRDO, COHR, LITE, CIEN, HIVE, NOW, ZS, CRM, SNOW, TSLA, GDDY, NOK, AMPX, ALMU in the last 24h.

**HIVE (background, Aug 17):** $350M/5-yr GPU cloud contract, ~$70M incremental ARR, targeting $200M total BUZZ HPC ARR by year-end. No October update found.

No other notable watchlist movers with identifiable catalysts in the last 24–72h.

---

## Context vs. Baseline

- DRAM cycle **decelerating** as expected into H2-2026 (+20% QoQ vs. +80%/+40% earlier). Still positive but the easy gains are past.
- HBM4 capacity ramp from all three suppliers tracking squarely to the correction-risk window (late-2026/2027). **Watch Q1-2027 HBM pricing closely.**
- Hyperscaler capex holding $720–745B aggregate; Q3 earnings updates (late October) are the next macro catalyst — any guide-down would be a regime change.
- Optical names have re-rated significantly YTD (LITE +183%); InP constraint is real and persisting into 2027.
- Solar Sec 232 tariffs: mixed — supports FSLR (US CdTe manufacturer), headwind for importers and residential installers.

| Solar tariffs | Dec 4 effective | Mixed (FSLR positive, installers negative) |
| Broad chip tone | Weak mid-Oct, NVDA -2.4% | Near-term bear |

---

## Most Important Development

**TrendForce's Oct 20 Q4-2026 DRAM print (+20% QoQ) marks the first clear deceleration signal, down from +80% and +40% in prior quarters.** Combined with all three HBM4 suppliers aggressively ramping capacity into year-end, this is the strongest data point yet supporting the baseline 'correction risk after 2026' thesis. The next binary catalyst: hyperscaler Q3 earnings (late October) — any capex guide-down would represent a regime change for the entire complex.
